result.comment: Three-story plan: scope check identity to snapshots, isolate foreground recovery, and preserve truthful execution diagnostics. Plan orphan recovery remains deferred. No open questions. Implementation and tests have not started. After factory publication and readiness, use /implement the three-story bug fix plan.

plan.summary: Three small repairs: allow reused check names across snapshots, isolate foreground recovery from other runs, and retain truthful execution diagnostics. Plan orphan recovery stays deferred. Reuse the current protocol and existing store/turn components.

stories.title: Allow different story snapshots to reuse check names

user_story.want: different stories to use the same check name without rejecting valid evidence
user_story.benefit: a completed story does not prevent later stories from being submitted
notes: Evidence inventory AC-001: real disposable SQLite upgrade/fresh/repeated-migration tests; existing store fixtures are available; implementation-revision backend proof only; new regression execution required.

Evidence inventory AC-002: store and submission/shared-result regression tests; existing fixtures and retained research probe are available; probe proves the old defect only; passing repair assertions required. No live nested-agent evidence is required.

acceptance_criteria.text: An additive migration makes retained checks unique by (run_id, snapshot_ref, reference) on fresh and populated databases. It preserves existing evidence, provenance, ownership, foreign keys and retained-byte accounting. Repeating migration is harmless.

Two stories in one run using build under distinct snapshots both preflight and submit successfully, and every production reader resolves the correct snapshot. Exact same-tuple replay is idempotent; changed content under that tuple conflicts. Wrong-snapshot and relabelled aggregate evidence are rejected. Exact request replay preserves its receipt identity.

tasks.description: Add the migration and update every retained-check writer/reader to require exact authorized snapshot identity, including reference-only and shared-result resolution.
Write and run real disposable SQLite and submission/shared-result regressions for migration, duplicate labels, immutable conflicts, replay and evidence ownership using ordinary Go tests.

architecture.summary: Keep exact check identity in the existing store API; turn supplies the authorized snapshot.

components.name: internal/store
components.responsibility: Own the additive embedded migration, exact check lookup and immutable evidence retention.

components.name: internal/turn
components.responsibility: Supply authorized snapshot identity in all submission and shared-result readers/writers.

interfaces.name: Retained-check access
interfaces.input: Context, run ID, snapshot reference and check reference; existing content for writes.
interfaces.output: The exact retained check or an ownership/immutable-conflict error.

constraints: No ambiguous run/check fallback or agent naming-prefix requirement.
Preserve single-connection SQLite, retained accounting, request replay and independent aggregate/story provenance checks.

decisions.decision: Scope check identity to the snapshot without extra issue/story columns or protocol fields.
decisions.reason: Snapshots already bind evidence ownership; the missing key dimension causes the collision.

stories.title: Keep broken recovery work from failing unrelated runs

user_story.want: each finishing run to handle only its own foreground recovery
user_story.benefit: unrelated broken work cannot discard a healthy run's result
notes: Evidence inventory AC-003: real store/turn paths with broken A, healthy B, distinct attempts and own-run failure; existing recovery/runner fixtures are available; controlled backend proof only; targeted passing regressions required.

Evidence inventory AC-004: real global recovery path with broken A and healthy C plus correlated diagnostics; existing fixtures available; no claim of live host capability; targeted passing regressions required.

acceptance_criteria.text: Broken pending work for run A cannot fail healthy run B through foreground submission, session Close, terminal Validate intake, Finish or harvest. Bound paths select only the trusted run/attempt; legacy Finish stays run-scoped. Discovery and lock-protected reloads respect that boundary. B keeps its own correlated result, and genuine failures belonging to B still surface.

Explicit daemon-wide maintenance continues from a broken receipt to healthy run C. Recovery errors identify the originating run, attempt, receipt and phase, plus story when present. Existing sequencing, authorization, replay and uncertain-effect recovery behavior remains effective.

tasks.description: Add store-owned scoped selection and explicit foreground recovery entry points; update submission, Close, terminal Validate and Finish discovery/reloads. Preserve explicit global maintenance and attribute its errors to originating work.
Write and run ordinary Go tests using real disposable SQLite and controlled runners for A/B isolation, attempt boundaries, local failures and global continuation to C.

architecture.summary: Use existing factory bindings to filter foreground recovery before processing; keep daemon maintenance explicitly global.

components.name: internal/store
components.responsibility: Select only authorized pending receipts/progress/effects for foreground processing.

components.name: internal/turn
components.responsibility: Apply scope consistently through recovery, Finish discovery and locked reloads; propagate only local errors.

components.name: internal/daemon
components.responsibility: Retain the explicitly global maintenance caller and existing scheduling.

interfaces.name: Foreground recovery
interfaces.input: Context and trusted run/attempt binding; legacy Finish's run ID.
interfaces.output: Recovery results and errors for that scope only.

interfaces.name: Global maintenance
interfaces.output: Continued processing with failures attributed to their originating receipts.

constraints: SQL remains in store; reuse existing locks, sequencing and transaction boundaries.
No new scheduler, retry loop, protocol identity field or Plan orphan lifecycle change.

decisions.decision: Enforce existing identity at internal recovery boundaries.
decisions.reason: The communication protocol already binds identity; global backend selection leaks failures across runs.

stories.title: Report the real execution and finalization failure

user_story.want: failure reports to retain what the agent actually did and identify the phase that failed
user_story.benefit: I can diagnose the real problem without losing execution evidence
notes: Evidence inventory AC-005: harvest tests with controlled startup/execution/interruption/finalization outcomes and sanitization assertions; existing diagnostic fixtures available; backend classification only; targeted passing regressions required.

Evidence inventory AC-006: existing successful Plan save/publication tests, focused store/turn/shared-result checks and make check; repository tests available; execute against final combined implementation. No live provider or deployment proof is claimed.

acceptance_criteria.text: Genuine startup failure, successful execution followed by local cleanup/finalization failure, failed execution with cleanup failure and interruption retain truthful causes and available process outcome, exit code and logs. Post-execution errors do not report that the agent never started. Diagnostics remain sanitized. Local factory failure still blocks workflow success and success-only save/publication.

Existing successful Plan save/publication behavior remains intact. Focused store, turn and shared-result regressions and repository-required make check pass on the combined repair before engineering completion.

tasks.description: Preserve available runner facts and failure phase through cleanup into harvest using existing error and diagnostic mechanisms.
Write and run controlled-runner harvest regressions covering startup, execution, finalization, interruption and sanitized diagnostics.
Run existing successful Plan save/publication regressions, focused affected-package tests and make check on the combined repairs; resolve failures and retain executed output.

architecture.summary: Retain actual subprocess facts while separately carrying the local factory failure into normal harvest reporting.

components.name: internal/turn/submission_runner.go
components.responsibility: Preserve the runner result and attach cleanup/finalization failure phase.

components.name: internal/turn/harvest.go
components.responsibility: Record actual process facts and truthful sanitized causes without granting false success.

interfaces.name: Runner-to-harvest result
interfaces.input: Available process result plus execution and/or factory-finalization error.
interfaces.output: Preserved process evidence and accurately attributed overall failure.

constraints: Reuse existing retained diagnostics and reporting.
Preserve interruption behavior, sanitization and existing success-only save/publication gates.

decisions.decision: Keep process outcome distinct from overall factory success.
decisions.reason: A successful subprocess can still have a real local finalization failure; neither fact should erase the other.
